question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Sajni had / interfere in / this matter.
solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: "**interfere in**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**had**" is a past tense auxiliary verb.
 
• In this sentence, "**interfered**" is the past participle form of the verb "**interfere**," which means to become involved in a situation or activity that affects it in a negative way.
 
• The verb "**interfere**" always takes the preposition '**with**' after it.
 
• So, the correct verb form should be "**interfere with**", not "**interfere in**".
 
• The error is in the preposition used after "interfere".
 
• The correct sentence would be "*Sajni had interfered with this matter.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**No error**" is not the correct answer as there is an error in the sentence.
 
• "**this matter**" is not an error as it is a correct noun phrase.
 
• "**Sajni had**" is not an error as it is a correct subject-verb construction.
